findings.rationale: Migration results are computed and validated from an earlier read, but the write phase never verifies that each target still has those bytes. A concurrent edit is silently replaced by the stale migration output.

Duplicate detection compares lexical PathBuf values, so aliases such as file.fsl and ./file.fsl reach the atomic writer as distinct entries for the same file, producing duplicate backups and commits with unsafe rollback behavior.

Document checking loads approval records without verifying signed-record signatures, trust keys, spec binding, claim-set binding, or reviewed digest. An artifact embedding a forged approval can therefore be regenerated from the same forged record and reported document_conformant.

The approval check returns nonzero only for signature-invalid. Other non-current evaluation states caused by spec, artifact, claim-set, generator, or reviewed-artifact drift still exit successfully, so CI gates can accept a stale approval.

Approval records persist user-supplied artifact, glossary, and evidence paths verbatim, then later resolve them as process-relative paths. Moving the record or running approval check from another working directory can read different files or fail despite unchanged approved inputs.

AI replay compares a declared field only when the log event also supplies it. Events omitting model, prompt, retriever, or output_schema—including an empty object—produce no findings and can be reported replay_conformant.

AiProjectSummary has room for only one component and the line scanner overwrites it as additional components are encountered. Earlier components cannot be selected or replayed, and fields left unset by the last component may be inherited from a preceding component.

Domain lowering exposes saga observe actions for awaited aggregate events, but replay handles a domain_event only by adding its name to an output set. It never steps the corresponding saga_*_observe_* action, leaving saga history/state unchanged while claiming the event was observed.

After a completion is rejected by the model, replay still inserts it into completed, removes its pending request, and records its outcome as observed. Subsequent diagnostics and pending_effects therefore describe a lifecycle transition that never occurred.

The return value of pending.insert is ignored, so repeated requests for the same effect and correlation collapse into one set entry without a finding. Replay can report conformance despite duplicate dispatch of an irreversible external effect.

When scope changes, new bounds are applied to the old model only if the same key appeared in the old verify block. Adding a bound for an already-existing type therefore leaves the old model at its old/default scope while the result claims comparison under the new scope, invalidating semantic-diff findings.

Multi-file domain scaffolds are written directly to their final destinations one at a time. Any later directory or write failure leaves earlier files updated and later files stale, producing an inconsistent generated project despite returning an error.
